contract: Compare stream count and the audio entry's DTS classification, integral rate and samples per access unit from codec parameters after a MOV open, without stream discovery or packet decoding.

Compare the candidate’s core-signalling verdict and either the coded DTS sampling frequency from ddts or, without an access-unit clock, the AudioSampleEntry rate. FFmpeg reports the DTS codec identifier and its public stream rate and frame size. A candidate entry refusal is distinct from a non-DTS entry.
The typed-format case compares the supplied format with the wire entry type on the candidate and with the opened stream’s public codec_tag on the reference.
Input loading and schedule parsing precede the operation. Both sides open, consume and release their readers inside it.

open_deviations.reading: A DTS-specific box shorter than its fixed fields
open_deviations.clause: ETSI TS 102 114 V1.6.1 Annex E §E.2.2.3.1: the fixed fields of ddts occupy 20 payload bytes
open_deviations.candidate: refuses core admission on the incomplete description
open_deviations.reference: can publish DTS codec parameters, including inferred rate or frame size, or fail the entire MOV open on a short record

open_deviations.reading: A zero DTSSamplingFrequency fails the sample entry here and the whole file in the reference
open_deviations.clause: ETSI TS 102 114 V1.6.1 Annex E §§E.2.2.2 and E.2.2.3.2: the coded frequency must designate the sampling rate at which the access-unit samples are counted; a zero frequency designates none and both sides refuse it, and neither Annex E nor ISO/IEC 14496-12 says whether one bad entry fails the movie
open_deviations.candidate: reports an unsupported core configuration for the entry with zero frequency

open_deviations.reading: MPEG-4 object type AA declares a DTS core and extension
open_deviations.clause: MP4 Registration Authority, Object Types table (A9–AC): AA denotes the core plus extension substream
open_deviations.candidate: reports eligibility for core inspection and 48000 Hz from the sample entry
open_deviations.reference: reports no DTS codec classification and no DTS clock

open_unimplemented.feature: The core check refuses a dtse entry: DTS LBR is not implemented
open_unimplemented.clause: ETSI TS 102 114 V1.6.1 Annex E Tables E-1 and E-2: dtse designates LBR in an extension substream without a core; FrameDuration code 3 is 4096 samples (E.2.2.3.2), which is what the reference reports: the input is valid
open_unimplemented.reference: reports generic DTS at 48000 Hz with 4096 samples

open_unimplemented.feature: The core check refuses a dtsx entry as unsupported where the reference reports no DTS
open_unimplemented.clause: ETSI TS 103 491 V1.2.1 §§B.2.2 and F.2.3: dtsx is DTS-UHD profile 2 and its entry carries udts, distinct from the DTS-HD coding names in ETSI TS 102 114 V1.6.1 Table E-1: both answers say the entry is no DTS core, and no clause decides between refused and not recognised
open_unimplemented.candidate: refuses the unsupported DTS-UHD tag for core playback
open_unimplemented.reference: reports no DTS codec classification for the fixture

open_unimplemented.feature: The core check refuses object types 0xAB and 0xAC: DTS extension substreams without a core are not implemented
open_unimplemented.clause: MP4 Registration Authority, Object Types table (A9–AC): AB declares an XLL-only extension and AC declares an LBR-only extension; ETSI TS 102 114 V1.6.1 clause 7.2 allows a stream of extension substreams alone, so the input is valid; both sides decline it, and no clause decides between refused and not recognised
open_unimplemented.candidate: reports unsupported core signalling for both known extension-only object types
open_unimplemented.reference: reports no DTS codec classification for either
